feedback: The check-in delivered on iteration 5 (mandatory checkin_every cadence) blocked the run pending a real human decision on devsystem.android_native_bridge: cargo-ndk vs UniFFI for the Rust->Android bridge. The operator answered directly (not via the pipeline's own channels this time, but in the driving conversation): UniFFI-generated bindings, not hand-written JNI -- matching the research doc's own lean (docs/android-native-bridge-options.md), citing UniFFI's real async support (matches ct-client's actual tokio/quinn-based async flow) and reduced hand-written FFI surface area for the code that will eventually handle key material/handshake state. cargo-ndk is still needed regardless, for cross-compilation. Plan for this iteration and the next: a minimal, honest spike first -- a trivial UniFFI-exported Rust function, cross-compiled via cargo-ndk, Kotlin bindings generated, wired into the Gradle build and called from MainActivity -- proving the toolchain works end to end in this actual environment BEFORE touching the real Noise_IK/Agent-Fabric code. Real-device/emulator execution can't be verified on this resource-constrained host (no working Android emulator available); build-time verification (assembleDebug packaging the .so + generated Kotlin compiling) is the honest scope for this slice.
